title: QuickServe: curated micro-utility gallery with safe dry-run and telemetry
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: oncall and SREs frequently reach for ad-hoc shell snippets or long runbooks during incidents. Those artifacts are brittle, often lack RBAC, and provide poor telemetry for post-incident analysis. QuickServe is a small curated gallery of permissioned, typed micro-utilities (single-purpose runlets) with enforced dry-run, structured inputs, and telemetry hooks. Goal: reduce mean time to safe remediation by providing discoverable, audited, and replayable tools that agents can run with confidence.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A gallery UI in the Ops Console listing curated micro-utilities with descriptions and required roles. 2) Each micro-utility executes with a mandatory dry-run mode that performs validation and emits a simulated output without side effects. 3) Execution requires a permission check (RBAC) and logs a structured telemetry event (run_id, user, params, dry_run_flag, result_code). 4) At least 6 pilot utilities (restart-service, db-schema-check, kv-prefix-flush-sim, memcache-evict, collect-debug-bundle, rollout-toggle-audit) implemented as first-class artifacts with PRs and tests. 5) End-to-end test harness that runs dry-run for each utility in CI and asserts no side effects. 6) Confluence doc and runbook linking for each utility.
